status: decision recorded for post-authoring repair; not a quota adjustment
rule: Taught recall and explanation: AO1. Consequential inference from supplied facts/data: AO2. Conducting, presenting or evaluating investigations and drawing from a specimen image: AO3. Bloom and command words follow the actual credited demand, not the card subtype.

decisions.reason: A single subtraction plus reading the sign of the result is applying a procedure, the same demand as the sibling CALC card labelled Apply; no pattern, relationship or structure is analysed. AO2 (B3) stays.
Ordering three decimals by place value is a routine number skill (Apply, arguably Understand), not analysis. Selecting from supplied values remains B (B1/B3).
Two routine fraction operations on supplied counts; the cognitive demand matches the Apply CALC siblings. AO2 stays.
Dividing a total in a given ratio is a standard procedure applied to supplied numbers; nothing is analysed. This is a maths-skills card, not the genetic-ratio boundary, so AO2 stays unchanged.
Same demand as the sibling CALC card 021 (solve x = y + z for one term), which is labelled Apply; the meaning given in the second blank is the definition of 'initial mass'.

Two unit conversions using known factors, with no data or context to interpret: Apply. B3 (manipulating numerical data) still fits, so AO2 is kept, though A2 (units and conventions) is a near boundary.
A single conversion followed by a direct size comparison is Apply. AO2 stays (B3).
Applying the quantity / unit labelling convention to named quantities involves no analysis. AO3 (C3, recording) stays.
Applying a recording convention and paraphrasing what it means is Apply (or Understand), not Analyse. AO3 (C3) stays.
A routine mean calculation, the same demand as CALC 003 (labelled Apply). AO3 stays because the objective is completing and processing practical tables (C3).
Dividing a supplied range into four equal steps is applying a scale rule; the learner does not choose a scale against data. AO3 (C3) stays.
Applying the axis-label and title conventions to quantities the prompt supplies is Apply. AO3 (C3) stays.

Recalling a plotting convention and its reason, with no data, is Remember/Understand, not Analyse. AO3 is kept because the objective is the Paper 3 graph-presentation convention, though A2 (conventions) is a near boundary.
Same demand as 040: applying labelling and title conventions. AO3 stays.
Making a measurement with an instrument is carrying out a procedure (Apply), not explaining one. AO3 (C2, observing and measuring specimens) stays.

AO2 is right: the learner processes supplied key information (B2/B4). But each description maps directly onto one branch per step, so the task is applying a procedure, not breaking down or relating information; the guidance credits only the correct reading of each branch.

The task is a calculation followed by a comparison; nothing is completed (no table or diagram to fill in), so 'complete' does not describe it. 'Calculate' is on the syllabus list and matches the guidance (marks for working out both lengths). AO2 and Analyse stay. Flag: changing the command word may change the tariff rules applied to this slot.
The learner breaks down supplied results (works out the 15 s and 21 s intervals) and judges whether they fit a model. That is analysis of data rather than applying a rule. AO3 (C3/C4) stays.

Parts (a)-(c) are recall and taught description; (d) applies taught osmosis knowledge to predict plasmolysis. No part asks the learner to break down data or relationships, so Analyse overstates the demand and Apply is the highest level reached. AO1+AO2 kept (see uncertainty). Note: 'state' fits only part (a); no single syllabus command word covers all four parts, so I propose no command-word change.

The three marks require a linked mechanism (emulsify, so surface area rises, so lipase acts faster), which is a taught explanation rather than recall of a single fact; comparable mechanism items here (3-324 PROC, 3-331 WHY, 3-337 WHY) are Understand. AO1 and command word are correct.

Three of the four marks reward observing and recording from a specimen image (outline as it appears in the photograph, vessel positions for that view, label-line conventions), which is the C drawing-from-specimen demand; only the labels are recall. The parallel root-section drawing item 3-355 is already AO3/Apply.

AO2 and Apply are right, but the task is to propose a likely explanation of a new situation, not to state main points; 'Describe a likely explanation' is a mismatch and the syllabus 'Suggest' fits this inference. Flag: changing to Suggest may change the tariff rules applied to this card (tariff currently 2).

The answer is the taught account that a donor must match or the kidney is rejected, and that dialysis removes urea in the meantime. The patient detail does not call for any new inference. The operator's review classes generic transplant/dialysis comparisons and mechanisms as A, and this item fits that ruling.

Each mark needs a causal reason (concentration gradient, particle size, equal concentration means no net diffusion), not a recalled name. That is taught understanding, so Understand fits better than Remember. The AO stays A.

The prompt asks 'describe why' and the marks reward reasons, which is what the syllabus means by Explain, not Describe ('state the main points'). The AO2 label is sound because the learner has to reason through a modified mechanism. FLAG: changing the command word may change which tariff rules apply. Other AO2 explain APP cards in this group (for example 3-050 and 3-080) also carry 2 marks.

'Describe why' asks for reasons, so Explain is the syllabus command word that fits. FLAG: this change may change the tariff rules. AO2 is kept but is a boundary: the reasoning is very close to the taught account in 3-102 (HIV passed on by shared needles), and a teacher could reasonably call it A.

Both marks reproduce the taught implications of self-pollination (no reliance on another plant or pollinator; less variation), the same points credited in A-labelled 4-034-EVAL; the scenario adds nothing to process. The operator review classifies taught self-pollination consequences as A.

The credited answer is the taught hormone role from 4-044-PROC and the A-labelled 4-066-WHY/4-068-WHY stated for its absence; no supplied data are processed and no inference beyond the rehearsed causal link is needed. Comparable 'why does X fail' items in this topic (4-066-WHY, 4-068-WHY) are already labelled AO1.

The prompt contains no investigation, measurement, data or method element; it asks only for the taught respiration/photosynthesis explanation. The practical objective it sits under does not by itself make it C (apparatus words alone do not suffice; here there are none).

AO2 (genotype inference, operator-settled B) and Bloom are kept. The prompt asks the learner to deduce and explain, not to describe; 'explain' (syllabus list) matches the justification mark. Flag: changing the command word may change the tariff rules for this slot.

The answer is the taught account of sigmoid-curve phases that the objective itself names (identify the phases, explain limiting factors). No values have to be read off the graph and nothing unfamiliar is supplied, so there is no information processing or new inference.

Command word only: the prompt asks 'Describe why...', which asks for reasons. The syllabus defines Explain as giving reasons and Describe as stating the main points. explain has the same modal tariff (2) as describe, so the 2-mark tariff should not change, but this departs from the work-order slot's command word (describe, from the objective's verb). The other fix is to reword the prompt as a 'Describe how...' task and keep describe. AO1 and Understand are correct for this taught account.
